title: Public Charge by Julissa Reynoso and Michael J Chepiga at The Public ...
transcript: Whether you find this play a riveting political drama or a tedious bore may depend on how much you know about the subject matter beforehand. Based on true events, Public Charge follows Julissa Reynoso working at the U.S. State Department during the Obama administration and trying to improve U.S.-Cuba relations. As an immigrant from the Dominican Republic who is well aware of the systems that divide us, she was seeking a way to make a difference and overhaul the policies that often guardrail our government from actually serving us. It's a solid premise for a play — a protagonist enters a highly complex and convoluted situation, attempting to do good but encountering obstacles and bureaucracy along the way. The way this piece plays out, however, is a pretty cut and dry telling of the events from her point of view — after all it is co-written by Julissa Reynoso herself. The other characters primarily serve as functional entities rather than real people, and the plot itself, though presumably very historically accurate, loses a lot of momentum in the final third. This is arguably more of a documentary piece than a political drama, and through that lens I felt it was actually pretty successful. As someone who wasn't familiar with this story, I definitely learned a lot and thought it was interesting. But if you're more well-read than I am and you're hoping for not just a rehash of what you may already know, this might come up short. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
